title: Data privacy
content:
## How we handle your data

When you build on Emergent, you're trusting us with your project code, chat history, environment variables, and any data your app generates. We take that responsibility seriously.

<Callout type="success" title="Your data is private by default">
Your projects, chat logs, code, and secrets are **never** shared with other users or used to train LLMs. We isolate every workspace and encrypt data in transit and at rest.
</Callout>

## Where your data lives

All project data — including source code, build artifacts, environment variables, and chat history — is stored on secure cloud infrastructure in the United States. We use industry-standard encryption (TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest) and follow AWS best practices for storage isolation.

Your MongoDB databases are hosted in the region you select at project creation time. By default, databases are created in `us-east-1`, but you can choose other regions if data residency is a concern. See [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) for configuration details.

## Who can access your data

<Steps>
<Step title="You and your workspace members">
Anyone you invite to your workspace can view and edit project code, inspect logs, and read chat history. Manage access carefully — there is no read-only role yet.
</Step>

<Step title="Emergent platform services">
Our backend services access your data to:
- Execute builds and deployments
- Stream logs and debugging output
- Generate AI-assisted code and fixes
- Route API requests to your deployed apps

This access is **automated and scoped** — no human Emergent employee views your data as part of normal operations.
</Step>

<Step title="Emergent support (with your consent)">
If you open a support ticket and explicitly share a project link or invite support staff to your workspace, our engineers may inspect logs, environment variables, and code to diagnose issues. We will **always ask permission** before looking at sensitive data.
</Step>

<Step title="LLM providers (anonymized context only)">
When you use AI features, we send code snippets and chat context to third-party LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.). These requests are anonymized and do not include your workspace name, email, or identifiable metadata. LLM providers process the data according to their own privacy policies; we do **not** opt your data into model training.
</Step>
</Steps>

## What we don't do

- **We don't sell your data.** Ever.
- **We don't train models on your projects.** Your code and chat logs stay out of any training pipeline.
- **We don't index your projects for search** outside your own workspace.
- **We don't retain deleted data indefinitely.** When you delete a project, we purge code, logs, and build artifacts within 30 days. Database backups expire according to the retention policy you set.

## Reducing exposure

If you're working with particularly sensitive data, consider these practices:

- **Use environment variables for secrets** rather than hardcoding them in source. These are encrypted at rest and never logged in plain text.
- **Limit workspace invitations** to team members who need access.
- **Rotate API keys regularly**, especially if a team member leaves or you suspect a leak.
- **Self-host sensitive databases** and connect via secure tunnel, rather than using the built-in MongoDB for regulated data.
- **Review deployed app permissions** — a public URL means anyone with the link can access your app's endpoints. Use authentication if you need to restrict access.

For more on preventing accidental data exposure in your app's public endpoints, see [Data leakage](/data-leakage).

## Questions about ownership

You retain full ownership of your code, designs, and data. Emergent claims no IP rights to what you build. For the legal details, see [Your data & ownership](/your-data-ownership).

<Note>
If you have specific compliance requirements (GDPR data processing agreements, HIPAA, SOC 2 attestation), reach out to our enterprise team — we offer tailored agreements for regulated industries.
</Note>
description: Where your data is stored and who can access it; addressing privacy worries.
